questions.question: A plane flies 100 km West, then it turns South and flies 150 km, then it turns West and flies 300 km, then it turns to its right and flies 150 km. Where is it now with reference to its starting position?
questions.questionHtml: A plane flies 100 km West, then it turns South and flies 150 km, then it turns West and flies 300 km, then it turns to its right and flies 150 km. Where is it now with reference to its starting position?
questions.solution:
Assuming ‘L’ as the starting position and ‘P’ as the ending position.

ON = 300 km.

ON = PM = 300 km.

LM = 100 km.

Thus, PL = PM + ML

= 300 + 100

= 400 km.

Thus, the plane is 400 km west with reference to its starting position.

questions.question: Arnav's birthday is on Tuesday 14th March. On what day of the week will be Pranay's Birthday in the same year if Pranay was born on 13th September?

questions.solution:
Arnav’s birthday = 14th March, Tuesday

Pranay’s birthday = 13th September

Days between 14th March - 13th September =

→ 17 (March) + 30 (April) + 31 (May) + 30 (June)+ 31 (July) + 31 (August) + 13 (September)

→ 183 days = 183/7 → 1 odd day

→ Wednesday

Hence, Pranay’s birthday will be on Wednesday.

questions.question: ______ being a higher category, is the assemblage of families which exhibit a few similar characters.
questions.questionHtml: ______ being a higher category, is the assemblage of families which exhibit a few similar characters.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Order.

Key Points

  • The eight main taxonomic ranks are:
    • Domain
    • Kingdom
    • Phylum or division
    • Class
    • Order
    • Family
    • Genus and
    • Species.
  • Each step down in the classification divides organisms into more and more specific groups.
  • Order is the taxonomic category which groups families that exhibit similar characteristics.
  • Biologists, such as Ernst Haeckel, Robert Whittaker, and Carl Woese tried to classify all living organisms into broad categories called kingdoms.
  • Further classification is done by naming the sub-groups at various levels- kingdom, phylum or division, class, order, family, genus, species.
  • This is also known as the Taxonomic hierarchy.
  • Taxonomic hierarchy - It is the process of arranging various organisms into successive levels of the biological classification either in a decreasing or an increasing order from kingdom to species and vice versa.

Additional Information

  • Kingdom - It is the highest level of classification. 
  • There are 5 kingdoms in which the living organisms are classified, namely, Animalia, Plantae, Fungi, Protista, and Monera.
  • Phylum - Organisms in a phylum share a set of characteristics that distinguishes them from organisms in another phylum. In botany, the term division has been used instead of the phylum.
  • Class - Class was the most general rank in the taxonomic hierarchy until phyla were not introduced. Kingdom Animalia includes 108 classes.
  • Order - It constitutes one or more than one similar family.
  • Family - It includes various genera that share a few similarities.
  • Genus - A group of similar species forms a genus.
  • Species - It refers to a group of organisms that are similar in shape, form, and reproductive features. There are about 8.7 million different species on earth.

questions.question: Sexual reproduction in Algae that takes place through fusion of two dissimilar size gametes is called?
questions.questionHtml: Sexual reproduction in Algae that takes place through fusion of two dissimilar size gametes is called?
questions.solution: Anisogamy, also known as heterogamy, is the form of sexual reproduction which involves the union or fusion of two gametes, which differ in size and/or form. In anisogamy, both gametes can be flagellated and therefore, motile or both may be non-flagellated. This latter condition occurs in some algae and plants.

questions.solution: In economics, short-run marginal cost is an economic concept that describes the cost of producing a small quantity of additional units of a good or service. The short-run marginal cost (MC) curve is U shaped. It first declines and then goes up at some point, and intersects the average total cost and average variable cost curves at their minimum points.

questions.question: The animals in which the body cavity is absent are known as _______.
questions.questionHtml: The animals in which the body cavity is absent are known as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Acoelomates.

Key Points

  • The animals in which the body cavity is absent are known as Acoelomates.
  • Example - flatworms and tapeworms, 
  • Acoelomates lack a fluid-filled cavity between the body wall and digestive tract. They exhibit bilateral symmetry.

Additional Information

  • Coelom is the principal body cavity in most animals, located between the intestinal canal and the body wall. 
  • Coelomates refers to the animals having fluid-filled body cavities called coeloms located within the mesoderm.
  • There are three different tissues layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm). The cells in each tissue layer become differentiated during development, becoming different tissues, organs, and a digestive tract.
  • Pseudocoelomates refers to animals having fluid-filled body cavity between endoderm and the mesoderm. Pseudocoelom means "false coelom" or "false cavity"
  • Wild refers to any living organism in its natural environment without interference of human beings.

questions.question: ______ is the number of individuals of the population who left the habitat and gone elsewhere during the time period under consideration.
questions.questionHtml: ______ is the number of individuals of the population who left the habitat and gone elsewhere during the time period under consideration.
questions.solution: The size of the population in a habitat keeps changing with time, depending on various factors including food availability, predation pressure and weather conditions. Immigration is the number of individuals of the same species that have come into the habitat from elsewhere during the time period under consideration. Emigration is the number of individuals of the population who left the habitat and gone elsewhere during the time period under consideration.

questions.question: According to the Second Law of Motion, for a given force, acceleration is inversely proportional to the _________ of an object.

questions.solution: Newton's second law of motion states that, “The acceleration of an object as produced by a net force is directly proportional to the magnitude of the net force, in the same direction as the net force, and inversely proportional to the mass of the object”.

questions.question: Of the 3 numbers whose average is 40, the first is 1/3 rd the sum of other 2. What is the first number?
questions.questionHtml: Of the 3 numbers whose average is 40, the first is 1/3 rd the sum of other 2. What is the first number?
questions.solution:
Let the first number be a

⇒ Sum of all the 3 numbers = 3 × 40 = 120

⇒ a = (1/3)(120 - a)

⇒ a = 40 - a/3

⇒ 4a/3 = 40

∴ a = 30

questions.question: A student has to secure 40% marks to pass. He gets 67 and fails by 13 marks. What is the maximum marks?
questions.questionHtml: A student has to secure 40% marks to pass. He gets 67 and fails by 13 marks. What is the maximum marks?
questions.solution:
Given: Passing % = 40%

Marks got = 67

Number of more marks needed to pass = 13

So, passing marks = 67 + 13 = 80

Let a be the maximum marks

⇒ a × (40/100) = 80

⇒ 0.4a = 80

∴ a = 200

Multiplying above equation by 2

⇒ -x + 5 + 6 = -5

⇒ -x = -16

∴ x = 16

questions.question: If the shopkeeper sells an item at Rs. 4400 which is marked as Rs 5000, then what is the discount that he is offering?
questions.questionHtml: If the shopkeeper sells an item at Rs. 4400 which is marked as Rs 5000, then what is the discount that he is offering?
questions.solution:
Let shopkeeper is offering x% of discount

So, Selling price = marked price × (1 - discount/100)

⇒ 4400 = 5000 × (1 - x/100)

⇒ 44/50 = 1 - x/100

⇒ x/100 = 1 - 44/50 = 6/50

∴ x = 6/50 × 100 = 12%

questions.question: In what ratio does the point T(x, 0) divide the segment joining the points S(-4, -1) and U(1, 4)?
questions.questionHtml: In what ratio does the point T(x, 0) divide the segment joining the points S(-4, -1) and U(1, 4)?
questions.solution:
Lets take that Point T divides SU in the ratio k1 : k2 , then the coordinates of point T are given by this formula:

⇒ xT = (k1xU + k2xS)/(k1 + k2) and yT = (k1yU + k2yS)/(k1 + k2)

⇒ xT = (k1xU + k2xS)/(k1 + k2) and 0 = (4k1 - k2)/(k1 + k2)

⇒ xT = (k1xU + k2xS)/(k1 + k2) and 4k1 = k2

Since, k1/k2 = 1 : 4 is satisfied by just one option, we don’t need to simplify xT term.

questions.question: The areas of two similar triangles ΔABC and ΔPQR are 36 sq cms and 9 sq cms respectively. If PQ = 4 cm then what is the length of AB (in cm)?
questions.questionHtml: The areas of two similar triangles ΔABC and ΔPQR are 36 sq cms and 9 sq cms respectively. If PQ = 4 cm then what is the length of AB (in cm)?
questions.solution:
Since, ΔABC and ΔPQR are similar triangles.

And Ar(ΔABC) = 4[Ar(ΔPQR)]

Let the ratios of base and height be a

And let the base and height of ΔABC be b1and h1

So, 1/2 × (b1)(h1) = 4[1/2 × (ab1)(ah1)]

⇒ a2 = 1/4

⇒ a = 1/2

So, PQ = a × AB

⇒ PQ = 1/2 × AB

∴ AB = 4 × 2 = 8 cm

questions.question: What is the reflection of the point (-0.5, 6) in the x-axis?
questions.questionHtml: What is the reflection of the point (-0.5, 6) in the x-axis?
questions.solution:
To find: reflection of the point (-0.5, 6) in the x-axis

⇒ the equation of line is: y = 0

The formula for finding the image of a point (x1, y1) to the line ax + by + c = 0 is given by:

(x - x1)/a = (y - y1)/b = -2(ax1 + by1 + c)/(a2 + b2)

Here, a = 0, b = 1 and c = 0

So, we have

(x + 0.5) = 0 and (y - 6) = -2(6)/(1)

⇒ x = -0.5 and y -6 = -12

∴ x = -0.5 and y = -6

questions.question: If the amount received at the end of 2nd and 3rd year at Compound Interest on a certain Principal is Rs 1,800, and Rs 1,926 respectively, what is the rate of interest?
questions.questionHtml: If the amount received at the end of 2nd and 3rd year at Compound Interest on a certain Principal is Rs 1,800, and Rs 1,926 respectively, what is the rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Let the principal be P

⇒ P(1 + r/100)2 = 1800

⇒ 1 + r/100 = √(1800/P)      ----(i)

Also, P(1 + r/100)3 = 1926

⇒ 1 + r/100 = (1926/P)1/3      ----(ii)

⇒ √(1800/P) = (1926/P)1/3

⇒ P = 1572

Putting the value of P in (i), we get

⇒ 1 + r/100 = √(1800/1572)

⇒ 1 + r/100 = 1.07

⇒ r/100 = 0.07

∴ r = 7%

Alternate Method

As we know,

Difference between 3rd year and 2nd year C.I = 1926 - 1800

⇒ 126

Rs. 126 is interest on Rs. 1800 then, Rate of interest:

⇒ (126/1800) × 100

⇒ 7%

∴ The Rate of interest is 7%.

⇒ 13 = a3 - b3 - 3(6)(1)

⇒ 1 = a3 - b3 - 18

∴ a3 - b3 = 19

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. hypnotist.

questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

At this moment that (1)/ terrible door burst noisily open and (2)/ banged for the wall. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Ans: 3

Bang means a strike or puts down forcefully or noisily against or on something. The word ‘for’ in the third part of the sentence makes the sentence grammatically incorrect. The correct sentence is: ‘At this moment that terrible door burst noisily open and banged against the wall.’
